## About This Course

-   Advanced statistical modelling and data analysis for real-world problems
-   Model building, diagnostics, interpretation, and selection
-   Case studies and real-world examples to connect statistical methods to practice
-   Statistical communication and critical thinking, with an emphasis on clearly interpreting and communicating results

## Course Motivation

-   Most of the students in this course will be graduating soon. Some of you will get a job in industry, others will pursue graduate studies, etc.
-   Regardless, it is likely that people who’ll be working with you expect you to be “experts” in statistics.
-   Most of the research questions you’ll be working with will be pretty straightforward and can be answered using prerequisites for this course.

<br>

::: {style="text-align: center; font-size: 1em;"}
To work with data in independent and responsible manner, it is critical that you know what’s really going on with the statistical models you use.
:::

## Do I Have the Appropriate Background?

The prerequisite for this course is **STA303: Methods of Data Analysis**.

<br>

This means that the following is assumed to have been learned:

-   some fundamentals: (maximum) likelihood, parameter estimation, hypothesis testing
-   linear models (e.g. least squares) and generalized linear models (e.g. logistic/Poisson regression)
-   R programming

## Course Materials & Important Links

**Textbook**: We will be using the following three textbooks: - \[ISL\] *An Introduction to Statistical Learning* by James et al. (https://www.statlearning.com) - \[LM\] Linear Models with R by Faraway (2nd edition) - \[ELM\] Extending Linear Models with R by Faraway (2nd edition)

<br>

## Tentative Course Schedule {.scrollable}

::: smaller
| Date | Topics | Suggested Reading | Assessments |
|:--------------:|:---------------|:---------------|:------------------------|
| Sept. 11 | **Statistical Modelling and Inference**<br>Study planning, data-generating process, statistical inference (Type I/II errors), simulation, sample size calculation | — | — |
| Sept. 18 | **Topics in Statistical Inference**<br>Multiple testing, family-wise error rate, false discovery rate, permutation methods | \[ISL\] Ch. 13 | Assignment 1 Released |
| Sept. 25<br>Oct. 2 | **Linear Models**<br>Least squares from likelihood and Gauss–Markov perspectives, weighted least squares, modelling considerations, model selection | \[LM\] Ch. 2, 3, 8.2, 10<br>\[ISL\] Ch. 3, 6.1 | Assignment 1 Due, Oct 2 |
| Oct. 9<br>Oct. 16 | **Generalized Linear Models**<br>Review of logistic and Poisson regression, likelihood-based inference, overdispersion, quasi-likelihood | \[ELM\] Ch. 2, 5, 8<br>\[ISL\] Ch. 4.1–4.3, 4.6 |  |
| Oct. 23 | **Midterm Exam** | — | Assignment 2 Released |
| Oct. 30 | **No class — Reading Week** | — | — |
| Nov. 6 | **Bayesian Thinking**<br>Prior and posterior distributions, choice of priors, Bayesian interpretation of penalized regression and GAMs | — | Assignment 2 Due |
| Nov. 13<br>Nov. 20 | **Random Effects Models**<br>Correlated data, generalized least squares, random effects, longitudinal data analysis, restricted maximum likelihood (REML), BLUP | \[ELM\] Ch. 10, 11 | Assignment 3 Released, Nov. 20 |
| Nov. 27 | **Penalized Regression**<br>Bias–variance trade-off, ridge regression, LASSO and variants, cross-validation, generalized CV, random-effects interpretation | \[ISL\] Ch. 6<br>\[ESL\] Sec. 7.10 |  |
| Dec. 4 | **Generalized Additive Models**<br>Basis functions, smoothing splines, generalized additive models | \[ELM\] Ch. 15<br>\[ISL\] Ch. 7<br>\[ESL\] Ch. 5 | Assignment 3 Due |
:::
